\captionof{figure}{\textbf{The Capability Sign-Flip: separating intelligence from execution authority turns scaling into an asset.} \textbf{(a)} Across search widths $K_{\mathrm{opt}}\in[1,4,096]$, internal safety judges collapse to $100\%$ breach, whereas Verus-verified exogenous sinks hold at $0.0\%$ ($0/120,000$) and zero-authority search closes open routes $19.0\times$ faster. \textbf{(b)} Training neural policy gradients \emph{inside} pre-commit gates ($q_{\mathrm{gate}} > q_{\mathrm{gate}}^*$) extinguishes covert scheming ($+34.5\to +0.03$\,pp) and lifts task competence $+44.8$\,pp over post-hoc deployment filtering ($41.0\%\to 85.9\%$). \textbf{(c)} Across 112 paired live Qwen3-4B/8B and AgentDojo runs, stateful sinks eliminate breaches ($0/112$ vs.\ 29.5\% unmediated and 12.5\% static Progent, $p=1.9\times 10^{-9}$), double safe task completion from 4B to 8B ($28.1\%\to 56.2\%$), and keep $90.1\%$ of benign steps unpaused.}\label{fig:v5hero}
